chunks.text: 69-year-old female, Service or Sales Worker, resident of Woodlands, Singapore.
Left wrist fracture in 2015, fully healed
Aspirin discontinued in 2021 due to resolved indication
Spinal anesthesia with general anesthesia as backup

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Liew, the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your knee surgery today. Let's go through some questions to make sure everything's in order, okay?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, doctor. Yes, sure thing. I'm ready when you are.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. First, can you tell me a bit about your knee problem? How long have you been having issues with it?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, about five years already. The pain got worse last year, can't even walk properly now. That's why I'm doing this surgery, right?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Now, let's go through your medications. You're on amlodipine for blood pressure, metformin and glipizide for diabetes, atorvastatin for cholesterol, omeprazole for stomach, and aspirin which was stopped recently?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, that's all correct. I take them every day except the aspirin, which I stopped a week ago like the doctor told me.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Any allergies to medications or other things?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Hmm, I don't think so. The records say no allergies, right?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Actually, I noticed the records say 'no known allergies,' but sometimes people might not mention things they think aren't important. Have you ever had a reaction to any medications, especially sulfa antibiotics?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh! Wait a minute... I had a rash once from some antibiotic. Was it sulfa? I think so. The doctor said it was an allergy, so I stopped taking that type since.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for mentioning that. So, a rash reaction to sulfa antibiotics. We'll make sure to note that properly. Any other reactions?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, that's the only one. I don't react to anything else.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Have you eaten or drunk anything since midnight? We need to confirm you're NPO for surgery.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, nothing since last night dinner. Just water for meds this morning, but that was hours ago.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Any previous anesthesia or surgeries?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Only once, a cataract surgery years ago. They gave me local anesthesia, I think. No problems then.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to know. Lastly, how's your mobility before surgery? Can you walk with assistance?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, with a walking stick. But the pain makes it hard, so I don't go out much now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Tan. We'll proceed with spinal anesthesia as planned, with general as backup. I'll see you in the operating room shortly.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Alright, doctor. Thank you for explaining everything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] fentanyl fifty micrograms intravenous

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] succinylcholine one hundred milligrams for intubation

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:07] endotracheal tube placed, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] arterial line placed

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] lactated ringers one thousand milliliters bolused for hypotension

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] mean arterial pressure thirty five, atropine one milligram given intravenously

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:25] phenylephrine twenty micrograms intravenous bolus administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Eh, still okay lah. Got some pain at the knee, but not too bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: What would you say your pain level is on a scale of 1 to 10?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe around 4 or 5? The nurse gave me some medicine earlier, so it’s better now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any nausea or vomiting since the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No nausea, but my mouth is very dry. Can I have some water?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Of course, we’ll get you some water. How’s your breathing? Any discomfort in your chest or throat?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing is fine, but my throat is a bit sore. Must be from the tube during surgery.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That’s normal. Do you remember anything about the surgery itself?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Nope, everything’s a blur. I think I slept through it all.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. For your health conditions—any issues with blood pressure or sugar levels today?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: BP was okay this morning, and my sugar’s been stable. Just worried about the knee, but it feels better already.
